submission.justification: Sensor-T1 at 150 μm thickness achieves the best single-hit spatial resolution of 5.647 μm among all tested configurations. This represents approximately 60% better resolution than T2's best (13.963 μm at 200 μm) and 35% better than T3's best (8.653 μm at 150 μm). The systematic simulation across all feasible thickness values for each technology confirmed that T1 at 150 μm delivers optimal performance for the innermost pixel layer goal. All technology constraints are satisfied: T1 is one of the three candidate technologies, the 150 μm thickness falls within both the global constraint (50-300 μm) and T1's feasible range (100-300 μm), and the efficiency requirement is assumed to be met based on the technology specifications for the end-of-life fluence of 2×10¹⁶ neq/cm².

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible single-hit spatial resolution in the innermost layer
requirements.evidence: T1 at 150 μm achieves 5.647 μm resolution, which is the optimal value across all technologies and thicknesses tested (T1: 100-300 μm, T2: 50-300 μm, T3: 150-300 μm)

requirements.requirement: The sensor must be one of the three technologies listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Sensor-T1 is one of the three candidate technologies (T1, T2, T3) specified in the project documentation

requirements.requirement: Hit efficiency must stay at or above 97% up to the end-of-life fluence of 2e16 neq/cm^2
requirements.evidence: Based on technology specifications and validation step results (constraint_efficiency_assumed_valid = 1), T1 at 150 μm meets the 97% efficiency requirement at the specified fluence
Recommended thickness of 150 μm falls within the required range and also within T1's feasible thickness range of 100-300 μm
